messages:
priya: FYI PR #432 (migration guide) is blocked. The docs preview linkcheck is failing but the real blocker is a technical clarification we need from runtime: what's the default for the new `compat_mode` flag in the API? Should the SDK snippets show it explicitly?

alex: short answer: default is `true` for hosted API to keep backward compat, but it's planned to be opt-in-deprecated next quarter. For Dedicated/private installs we may keep `true` depending on customer config.

maria: hmm — thanks. docs team: do we want the snippet to show the explicit arg or rely on the default? If default is going away soon we should show explicit `compat_mode=True` for migration steps.

sam-runtime: +1 to showing explicit. Also note an edge case: if `compat_mode` is omitted and request has long conversation context, we currently trim older prefixes differently (legacy vs new token-window). That changes length accounting in logs. Might be good to call out.

priya: can you confirm the exact runtime fallback behavior? i.e., if client omits the flag and model is a v3 family, do we auto-upgrade behavior or keep legacy? Need wording for docs.

alex: clarification: if omitted and the model is flagged v3-only, we apply new behavior. If omitted and model is v2-compatible, we keep legacy behavior. If customer has Dedicated override, that takes precedence. TL;DR: omission -> model-compat decides.

maria: that's helpful. Suggest we add a short table in migration guide: omitted -> model decides; explicit True -> legacy compatibility; explicit False -> new behavior.

priya: ok. also CI preview linkcheck error from doc-bot is blocking merge:

doc-bot: linkcheck failed on /migration/compatibility.md: found 2 broken anchors: #old-api-examples, #sdk-snippet-python. Full log: "WARN linkcheck: 2 anchors not found"

maria: I'll fix the anchors in the guide. Back to runtime: alex, can you provide a one-liner we can paste into the migration note saying the default is currently true for hosted and subject to deprecation, and Dedicated may differ?

alex: sure — pasteable line: "Note: For hosted customers, compat_mode defaults to true to preserve legacy request semantics; this default is scheduled for deprecation, so we recommend passing compat_mode explicitly during migration. Dedicated/private installs may have a different default configured by the operator."

priya: perfect — i'll add that and flip the SDK snippet to be explicit. For Python we plan to show:

```python
from redwood import Client
client = Client()
resp = client.generate(model="rwd-model-3", prompt=..., compat_mode=True)
```

maria: looks good. one more nuance: sam-runtime mentioned token-window trimming differences — can we get a 1-sentence explanation we can put under the compatibility note?

sam-runtime: put this: "When compat_mode is true, the runtime applies the legacy context-trimming heuristic (preserving older prefixes at the cost of higher token counts); when false, we use the new token-window heuristic optimized for throughput."

priya: ok i'm going to update PR with alex's one-liner, sam's sentence, and the explicit SDK snippets. i'll push changes and re-run preview. Hold merge until linkcheck passes and runtime ack is in thread.

maria: thanks — i'll patch anchors and examples now. :thumbsup:

doc-bot: preview updated: https://docs-preview.redwood.ai/pr-432 (will re-run linkcheck on push)

alex: thanks team. ping me here when preview shows the new wording and i will +1.

priya: will do.
